source.title: How To Match Clothes and Shoes For Guys: Outfit Color Guide
source.author: FashionBeans

tips.text: Choose solid-coloured shoes over multicoloured ones when you want to look smart.
tips.why: A single colour reads cleaner and more formal.

tips.text: Darker shoes are dressier and more versatile than lighter ones.
tips.why: Dark leather pairs with more outfits and formal settings.

tips.text: Judge a shoe's formality by shape and decoration as well as colour: a sleek chocolate oxford can be dressier than a plain black derby.
tips.why: Broguing and chunky shapes relax a shoe; sleek closed lacing dresses it up.

tips.text: Treat trainers by their own rules: white trainers suit nearly everything, while white dress shoes look odd.
tips.why: Sneaker conventions differ from those of leather dress shoes.

tips.text: Keep leather shoes polished with a matching or neutral polish; scuffs spoil any colour.
tips.why: Worn-looking shoes drag down the whole outfit.

tips.text: Let bright or colourful shoes be the loudest thing you wear, keeping the rest of the outfit neutral.
tips.why: Several strong colours compete and look messy.

tips.text: Wear black shoes with black suits and tuxedos, and with grey or charcoal suits in formal offices.
tips.why: Black is the most formal shoe colour.

tips.text: With jeans, choose black derbies or Chelsea boots rather than black oxfords.
tips.why: Oxfords are too dressy for denim and casual trousers.

tips.text: Don't wear black leather shoes with shorts.
tips.why: The combination looks like a school uniform.

tips.text: With colourful chinos, soften black shoes by choosing loafers, cuffing the hem and skipping socks.
tips.why: Formal black lace-ups look heavy against bright casual trousers.

tips.text: Brown shoes suit almost everything except black suits and the most formal offices.
tips.why: Brown is less formal than black but far more versatile.

tips.text: Keep brown shoes a couple of shades away from brown trousers instead of matching them closely.
tips.why: A near-match looks accidental; a clear contrast looks intended.

tips.text: Brown shoes with black jeans are risky; if you try it, choose a very dark brown or boots.
Use oxblood shoes like brown ones for more personality: derbies are the most versatile, penny loafers suit summer.
tips.why: Oxblood goes with navy, jeans and chinos but stands out more.

tips.text: Treat tan as the most casual brown: best in brogues, boots and suede with jeans and chinos.
tips.why: Light brown reads relaxed and lightens an outfit.

tips.text: With shorts, wear laceless or suede shoes such as loafers rather than lace-up leather.
tips.why: They match the relaxed feel of shorts.

tips.text: Avoid shiny blue leather shoes; blue works in suede or nubuck, such as navy chukkas with jeans.
tips.why: Glossy blue looks try-hard, while blue suede looks relaxed.

tips.text: Clean, logo-free white leather trainers can work with a suit if you swap the shirt and tie for a roll-neck or polo.
tips.why: Dressing down the top matches the casual shoe.

tips.text: Keep white trainers spotless with protective spray and wipes, and never wear battered trainers with tailoring.
tips.why: Their appeal depends on looking clean.
